EU Maintains Freeze on €210 Billion in Russian Assets Pending Reparations

03 Nov 2026, 06:31 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

Image: The Times of India · Photo source · Resized and letterboxed to 16:9; no AI generation

Key takeaways European Policy on Frozen Assets The European Union continues to hold approximately €210 billion in Russian sovereign assets under restriction. Kaja Kallas, the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, stated that these funds will remain froze

European Policy on Frozen Assets

The European Union continues to hold approximately €210 billion in Russian sovereign assets under restriction. Kaja Kallas, the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, stated that these funds will remain frozen until Moscow commits to providing reparations for the damages caused in Ukraine.

Status of Member State Support

Kallas emphasized that all 27 member states of the European Union are in agreement regarding the necessity of keeping these assets frozen. However, internal discussions persist regarding the legal and practical mechanisms for utilizing the interest or principal from these assets to support Ukraine.

  • Policy Stance: The EU leadership rejects proposals involving the territorial surrender of Ukraine as a path to peace.
  • Geopolitical Concerns: Kallas expressed caution regarding potential policy gaps between Washington and Brussels, noting that such divisions may be viewed as advantageous by the Kremlin.
  • Legal Challenges: Russia has officially challenged the asset freeze through judicial channels, characterizing the seizure or use of its funds without explicit consent as a violation of international law.

Verifying the Situation

Official statements from the European Commission and the European External Action Service (EEAS) serve as the primary sources for updates on asset management policy. Observers can monitor the EU’s official press releases for further developments on how these frozen funds are eventually allocated or managed in the context of the ongoing conflict.
